notes: Get around by bike or on foot; the GVB day pass costs 9 EUR, and the train to Schiphol takes 15 minutes. Don't walk in the bike lane (cyclists will ring their bells).
Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum, Anne Frank House: timed tickets online only; Anne Frank tickets are released 6 weeks ahead on Tuesdays at 10:00.
Winter is 3-7°C with rain: plan around museums and brown cafés, and catch the Amsterdam Light Festival in December. March to May is Keukenhof tulip season.
Eat stroopwafel hot at the market, herring at the stand and bitterballen in a brown café; coffee is 3.5 EUR, beer 5 EUR.
A coffeeshop is not a cafe; photography is banned in the Red Light District. Round up the bill when tipping.
Take the Sprinter train from Centraal to Zaanse Schans (20 minutes); arrive before 10:00.

stops.name: Rijksmuseum
stops.tips: Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer; book a timed ticket online, opens at 09:00, don't miss the library.

stops.name: Van Gogh Museum
stops.tips: Sunflowers and Almond Blossom; online tickets only, they sell out 3-7 days ahead.

stops.name: Museumplein Piknik
stops.tips: Pick up sandwiches at Albert Heijn and eat on the lawn; a paddling pool in summer, an ice rink in winter.

stops.name: Vondelpark
stops.tips: The city's main park; rent a bike, and catch the open-air theatre in summer.

stops.name: De Pijp & Albert Cuyp Markt
stops.tips: Amsterdam's biggest street market; try the stroopwafel stall (Rudi's) and the cheese.

backups.name: Moco Museum
backups.tips: Banksy and modern art; a good fallback if you have no Van Gogh ticket.

backups.name: Bakers & Roasters De Pijp
backups.tips: Brunch; an alternative to the picnic.

stops.name: Anne Frank House
stops.tips: Online only; tickets are released 6 weeks ahead on Tuesdays at 10:00. If sold out, check the daily cancellation release time.

stops.name: Westerkerk
stops.tips: The church where Rembrandt is buried; tower climbs run in summer.

stops.name: Jordaan Streets
stops.tips: Hofje courtyards (Karthuizerhof), the Prinsengracht canals, and Noordermarkt on Saturdays.

stops.name: Winkel 43
stops.tips: Amsterdam's most famous apple pie; on the corner of Noordermarkt.

stops.name: Café 't Smalle
stops.tips: A canalside brown café (traditional pub) open since 1786; drink a beer on the jetty.

backups.name: Café de Prins
backups.tips: A brown café opposite the Anne Frank House, good for lunch.

backups.name: Houseboat Museum
backups.tips: Life aboard a canal boat; in the Jordaan.

stops.name: Dam Square & Royal Palace
stops.tips: Tour the Royal Palace interior; the square is calm in the morning.

stops.name: Begijnhof
stops.tips: A hidden courtyard with a wooden house; quiet.

stops.name: Bloemenmarkt
stops.tips: The floating flower market; tulip bulbs make a good souvenir.

stops.name: Foodhallen
stops.tips: A food market in a former tram depot; try bitterballen (fried meat croquettes) and Vietnamese food.

stops.name: Canal Cruise
stops.tips: A 1-hour open boat (Those Dam Boat Guys / Flagship); the UNESCO canal ring in sunset light.

backups.name: Amsterdam Museum
backups.tips: The city's history; next to Begijnhof.

stops.name: Hortus Botanicus
stops.tips: A botanical garden from 1638; it has a butterfly greenhouse.

stops.name: Artis Zoo
stops.tips: A city-centre zoo with a planetarium.

stops.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
stops.tips: A brewery beneath a windmill; order the cheese platter and IJwit.

stops.name: Oosterpark
stops.tips: The park in the east; next to the Tropenmuseum.

stops.name: De Hallen Kino
stops.tips: A cinema and boutiques in a former tram depot; a good rainy-day option.

backups.name: Tropenmuseum Cafe
backups.tips: The cafe of the world cultures museum.

backups.name: NEMO Science Museum Roof
backups.tips: The free rooftop terrace of the ship-shaped museum; views over the harbour.

stops.name: Centraal Ferry Buiksloterweg
stops.tips: A free ferry from behind the station; 3 minutes.

stops.name: A'DAM Lookout
stops.tips: An observation deck on the north bank with the Over the Edge swing.

stops.name: EYE Filmmuseum
stops.tips: The white bird-shaped building; exhibitions and a cafe, with canal views.

stops.name: NDSM Werf
stops.tips: Street art and container cafes in a former shipyard; take ferry 906.

stops.name: Pllek NDSM
stops.tips: A restaurant in shipping containers; deckchairs on the beach and views of the IJ.

backups.name: Café de Ceuvel
backups.tips: A sustainable canalside cafe; in Noord.

backups.name: Noorderpark
backups.tips: The northern park; an alternative to NDSM.

stops.name: Zaanse Schans Windmills
stops.tips: 20 minutes by train (Zaandijk); working windmills (entry 5-6 EUR) and green wooden houses. Go before the morning tour buses arrive.

stops.name: Catharina Hoeve Cheese Farm
stops.tips: Cheese making and tasting; free.

stops.name: Zaanse Schans Clog Workshop
stops.tips: A demonstration of wooden shoe making.

stops.name: De Hoop op d'Swarte Walvis
stops.tips: A historic restaurant in Zaandam; fish and Dutch cuisine.

stops.name: Keukenhof
stops.tips: A tulip garden open 19 March-10 May only (in other months, go to Haarlem); 7 million flowers, book tickets online.

backups.name: Volendam & Marken
backups.tips: A fishing town and an island; an alternative to Haarlem.

stops.name: De 9 Straatjes
stops.tips: Nine streets of vintage shops, design stores and canal corners.

stops.name: Stubbe's Haring
stops.tips: A herring stand on a canal corner; eat it with onion and pickles, a Dutch ritual.

stops.name: Van Stapele Koekmakerij
stops.tips: One type of cookie only (white chocolate); expect a 20-minute queue.

stops.name: Amsterdam Centraal
stops.tips: 15 minutes by train to Schiphol; time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Spui Book Market
backups.tips: The Friday book market; an alternative to the streets.
